question: GQ-006
subject: "the residual is permanent" was a phrase, not a measurement
what_i_had_been_repeating: the 22.6 GB passage index has a permanent unverified residual
what_held: pragma integrity_check still cannot finish over USB — killed at 45s with no output. That limit is real.
what_did_not_hold: "cannot run a full integrity check" is not "cannot verify". I had been treating one pragma's limit as the whole verification story.
why_the_number_matters: 1.57% is a very different claim from "unverified", and the verifier now prints it on every run

a_bug_in_my_own_edit.what: set passage_ok=0 when an endpoint is unreadable — but a later line reassigns passage_ok from the band result alone
a_bug_in_my_own_edit.consequence: an unreadable endpoint would have reported SUCCESS
a_bug_in_my_own_edit.caught_by: reading the order of the assignments rather than trusting the edit
a_bug_in_my_own_edit.fix: a separate endpoints_ok flag; both conditions must hold

fifth_want_list_complete.note: every failure across five want-lists has been transient — not one book permanently unavailable

the_italian_filter_proved_itself: "The travels of Sig. Pietro della Valle" fetched correctly — the two-marker threshold spared an English book with an Italian name

a_concurrency_collision_found_by_running.what: npm run verify exited 1 with "database is locked (5)" while the background rebuild held a write lock
a_concurrency_collision_found_by_running.why_it_matters: a gate that fails because another process is mid-write reports a defect that does not exist — the fastest way to train a reader to ignore it
a_concurrency_collision_found_by_running.fix: corpus-integrity now reports skipped:true with the reason and an explicit "NOT a pass"
a_concurrency_collision_found_by_running.verified: reproduced live against the running rebuild
